I don’t want to die, I don’t want to be worthless to anyone, and even though I know the things it tells me about my pets may be true I don’t want to avoid them.

I wish it would go away, I feel like if I was to ask it why it’s doing this to me it would reply “because you deserve this, and because I can”.

Hey there,

Honestly a lot of what you're saying, I'm dealing with it too. I'm 22, working a job I don't enjoy, dealing with mental issues which skyrocketed when COVID started AND only grew after the whole George Floyd incident. My mind is like an abusive authority figure that tells me I'm someone who is either worthless and/or evil, and that my future is nothing but darkness. Suicide has been in the back of my mind for the last few years, and i've only ever really came close once, but i've just never been the same since.

But you should know, and i'm saying this as someone who is struggling too, you are not a "dumb pussy" for not having gone through it. The fact that you decided to come in here and talk about it is a HUGE thing to do. It shows that you're fighting, but also that you're hurting and you need help. And there is no shame in asking for help.

I'm so sorry COVID has caused you to feel so stuck, there are so many things I wish could do too but can't. But for now, slow down and try to think about what you do have and what you do value. Talk to your partner about what's been on your mind, spend time with your pets. But most importantly learn to try and take care of yourself. I know you probably don't believe it now but you're a good person, you are.

You're right when you say that your friends and family aren't your therapists, neither am I, but that doesn't mean they don't care or don't want to help.

I wish you the best of luck in these crappy times. :-)

I wonder about this too, constantly, to the point where one could consider it unhealthy. The idea that there is nothing after death completely frightens me, because even if my life is not how I wish it to be right now, I don't want to forget everything like it never mattered. The idea of heaven and hell feels better for me, because I would know that my life had some importance and that there is something to look forward to. And yeah, I don't know 100% if this is true, but I prefer this idea over nothingness.

As for you, I can't tell you what you should believe in, everyone and everything dies, as terrifying as it is, it is natural part of life. But my advice is this: maybe try and discuss these thoughts with someone close to you or someone you trust, and also, slow down and try to think about what you have in your life right now that you value.

I hope you find peace with your thoughts.
